summary: The article explores how ancient folklore about death omens and ancestral spirits is being woven into modern life, from fashion and architecture to jewelry, social media, and festivals. It pairs historical beliefs (Roman owl omens, Scottish door knocks, Dia de los Muertos, Qingming, Dreamtime) with a series of dated 2023 examples of contemporary creators. It also notes a scholarly debate on the neurological basis of afterlife visions that does not invalidate spiritual beliefs.
one_line: Death omens and ancestral spirit folklore are being reinterpreted in 2023 fashion, design, jewelry, tech, social media, and festivals.
key_facts: Romans observed birds to predict events, often seeing an owl during daylight as a portent of death.
In Scottish lore, a knock at the door with no one there signals impending death in the household.
On October 7, 2023, Laura Benson, a 32-year-old fashion designer from New York City, launched a line inspired by death omens, with the runway show "Omens in Ocher".
Dia de los Muertos (Mexico) and the Qingming festival (China) are cited as practices honoring ancestors.
On September 15, 2023, Daniel Thompson, a 40-year-old software developer from Toronto, turned his ancestors' stories into a 3D virtual reality experience.
DNA ancestry testing began mainstream popularity in the early 21st century.
Indigenous Australian Dreamtime stories teach about life and the ancestral realm.

On November 12, 2023, anthropologist Dr. Lisa Martinez published an article on the neurologic basis of afterlife visions, encouraging people to embrace cultural lore while understanding psychological and physiological underpinnings.
Architect Emily Harris unveiled a Chicago project with 'spirit doors' on September 3, 2023, inspired by traditional Japanese 'spirit pathways'.
On September 20, 2023, entrepreneur Alex Kim launched the jewelry line "Eternal Echoes" with personalized heritage-based pieces.
Hashtags #AncestralGuidance and #ModernMyths have surged on Instagram and TikTok.
Cultural blogger Kevin Sanchez started a viral series on November 1, 2023, exploring death omens in various cultures.
The "Luminous Spirits" festival on October 31, 2023, in San Francisco combined Day of the Dead iconography with digital light displays.
